summary: Newton is a tight worker-placement-adjacent game where you place cards on a shared board to trigger actions (buying goods, researching theories, moving your pawn, building machines) but must leave one card behind each round, permanently shrinking your options as the game progresses. It's a dense, efficient engine-builder with a satisfying tech-tree feel and almost no direct conflict, just competition for the same spaces.
praised: Elegant, tightly-interlocking action system where every choice has an opportunity cost
Strong sense of progression through the technology/discovery tracks
High replayability due to variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Good scaling and satisfying puzzle at 2 players especially
criticised: Steep rules overhead and iconography-heavy board that's intimidating for new players
Can feel dry or overly mechanical/spreadsheet-like with a thin scientific theme
Analysis paralysis potential given the many interlocking options each turn
First game often spent just learning what's possible before real strategy emerges

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light space/resource competition

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple tracks (theories, discoveries, machines, end-game bonuses, leftover resources), rewarding an efficient, diversified engine over a single dominant strategy
